findings.text: follow-on: the 300-cell row's serialized-proto cell reads "3.74 GiB (put refused)", but the cited source (docs/figures/millisecond-converged-solve/compile-memory/report.md:17,53-63) gives 461.7 MB at 300 and states it IS stored and retrieved; the value belongs to the 1,000-cell row, and it contradicts the report's own section-3 point 3 (breach already at >=1,000 cells).

follow-on: the serialized-program scaling law is labelled N^1.24, inconsistent with its own cited points (3.74 GiB@1,000 -> 19.2 GiB@2,500 implies ~1.79), with the source's "~cells^1.8", and with the section-3 projection values (~14/44/104/247 GiB imply ~1.5). The label, not the row's existence, is the defect.
